== Original post ==

'''World Champion LS: Savrip is a BEAST'''
* '''Author:''' Brandon "Jedi Genius" Schele
* '''Published:''' August 24, 2004
* '''Rating:''' 4.97
* '''Description:''' Fairly standard TRM deck I used on Day 2 and Day 3 of the World Championship to take home the title.

=== Strategy ===

This is what I ran on Day 3. The changes I made from Day 2 to Day 3 were:

In Day 2(and out for Day 3):

A Jedi's Resilience

Were You Looking For Me?

Goo Nee Tay

Sorry About The Mess & Blaster Proficiency

It Can Wait

In Day 3:

Escape Pod(V)

Sabotage(V)

Clash Of Sabers

Grimtaash

Control & Tunnel Vision

As for the starting effects, you choose them depending on your match up. If you need a BG site, start Insurrection & Aim High. If they're going to occupy a non-battleground for a while, start For Luck(V)(i.e. against Walkers and Senate). I'm sure most of you can figure out which to start in whichever matchups, but the "default"(if it can be called such a thing) start is Wokling(V) and Insurrection & Aim High.

This is the TRM I played on Day 2 and 3 of worlds, going 2-1 Day 2 losing only to Raveling's CCT, and 3-1 Day 3 losing only to Nick Jones's HD by 6 due to the fact that I activated a whole 4 force the first 5 turns of the game(can't really do too much with that, can you?). On Day 2 it beat Reinhold's BHBM by 28 and a timed win against Phillip Aesen's Walkers by 19. Day 3 it beat Lee Edwards's SYCfrimbazel) by 28, Brian Hunter's CCT by 24, and Reid Smith's AOBS by 16 in the final. It's a solid deck that can obviously stand up to a large variety of decks.

So why TRM over a "solid" deck that sets up itself and sticks to it's own plan? It's simple: Because that's what just about every dark deck does. And as it turns out, the DS usually wins that because they get not only bigger drains, but direct damage AND usually has the room in the deck to have characters/ships to disrupt YOUR plan. Hence the need to play a reactive deck like TRM.

I know TRM has been done over and over again, so I'll just discuss some card choices:

Honor Of The Jedi x2 - This is Pistone tech. He was the one who told me to play it, I was originally running Insight and Honor, and changed it to this and added For Luck(V) as a possible starting effect. No one expects this.

Wedge RSL - Cancelling a 2nd destiny in space is HUGE against most decks, since the DS has so many ways to draw more than one destiny(obviously have him pilot with Corran).

Only 1 Goo Nee Tay - On Day 2, I found that this card wasn't all that important in most of my matchups. It's practically useless against Walkers, and CCT doesn't deploy too many guys anyway to have this be effective. Because of this, I dropped the 2nd Goo Nee Tay for Day 3.

It Can Wait - Obviously this only made the cut Day 2, but it can help give you a chance to beat up the opponent by playing this on some support guy for someone on table. Dropped for Day 3 in favor of I believe Grimtaash(actually, It Can Wait was one of the first cards out, that and A Jedi's Resilience for the Escape Pod(V)).

Mantellian Savrip - I know this card is obvious, but I have to say this right now: IT IS THE BEST CARD IN THE GAME. It is the one card that allows you to not over deploy, it allows your space fleet to always stay in tact. It allows your characters to never die unless they get hit. It prevents you from almost EVER taking overflow. This card is so good that I HAD to play at least 1 puller, and if I had room, I'd play 3 Escape Pod(V)'s just to get this card out. Obviously you protect it by grabbing Masterful Move and then playing Sense on it, even if it means you have to lose force to do so. This card is just that damn good.

Sabotage(V) - With word of Laser Cannons being played to shoot down my capitals, combined with the fact that it can cancel the Chamber Console against CCT(effectively preventing them from pulling effects from reserve), I figured it was worth a slot. At worse, it cancels a permanent weapon targetting at the same site as Corran or Boussh, so that's not too bad.

Clash Of Sabers - This was SATM&BP Day 2, but I switched it out for the guaranteed exclusion in hopes of creating beats. I never used this card though except to cancel Hunter's POTF on the Security Tower against his CCT, which obviously wasn't the "intended" use, but it was definitely good enough for me.

Matchups with this deck is fairly unnecessary, you just react to what your opponent does. If they don't play a BG system, and not much space(that you can tell), deploy Kessel and go to it with a drain. Need a BG site AWAY from where they are? Play the Coruscant DB and move Yoda over(make sure savrip is out). This deck is just good, and gives you a good chance against practically everything(except Senate;-) ). Not really an out-of-the-ordinary TRM, but still a very good deck and most likely the best option the LS has right now.

As with the Senate deck, if there are any questions about the deck, feel free to dmail me or just post them in the review and I'll update the strategy.

Brandon Schele

2004 SW:CCG World Champion
